Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks for taking the time today 	6 great discussion on the integration patterns and evaluation goals. Quick recap from our side and a proposed observability-focused plan for the POC so your engineers can validate performance and reliability over the trial.

High-level POC goals / success criteria (proposed)
- Functional: Redwood inference endpoints integrated with FinTechX flow for 10-20 TPS sustained over sample traffic.
- Performance: P95 latency < 250ms for the primary prompt, error rate < 0.5%, no regressions in output quality vs baseline.
- Economics: token cost per request within the expected budget (we'll provide per-run estimates).
- Observability: Enough telemetry to validate latency/throughput, model fallbacks, and cache effectiveness.

Proposed timeline
- Week 0 (next week): Kickoff + access and network checks
- Week 1: Integration + basic telemetry (traces + request logs)
- Week 2: Dashboards + load validation
- Week 3: Final evaluation & handoff

Immediate asks
1) Please confirm your engineering point-of-contact for the POC (ideally someone who can join the kickoff).
2) Confirm whether you want logs exported to Splunk, S3, or a different system.

Attached is a short draft observability plan (20270405-redwood_poc_observability_draft.pdf) that outlines recommended dashboards and instrumentation. I marked proposed owners next to each item.

Next steps: If this looks good we'll lock the kickoff time and share a concise mutual action plan + access checklist.

Thanks,

Great 	6 thanks Alice and Ryan. Looping Dev and Marissa to confirm owners and implementation approach.

Below are the concrete observability items we recommend for the POC (we'll provide dashboards and a short instrumentation guide):

Dashboards (suggested out-of-the-box views)
- Overview: request rate (RPS), average latency, P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, model version in use, active connections
- Cost/Economics: tokens per request, tokens per minute, estimated $/hour and $/request (sampled)
- Caching & KV: prefix cache hit rate, KV cache size, cache eviction counts
- Model routing & fallback: counts of fallback to smaller/cheaper models, fallback latency impact
- Resource utilization: GPU GPU% (if Dedicated), CPU, memory per pod

Tracing & Logs
- We instrument using OpenTelemetry-compatible spans for request start/finish, model inference, KV cache lookup, and any external calls. Traces will include a request_id that ties to logs.
- Request logs: minimal structured logs (json) with request_id, user_id (if provided), model_version, prompt_length, tokens_generated, latency_ms, status.
- Export: we can push logs to your Splunk HTTP ingest (we need endpoint + token). If preferred we can write to S3 (parquet/json) on a schedule.

Metrics & Alerts (suggested SLIs/SLOs)
- SLI: P95 latency 	6 Alert if > 300ms for 10m window
- SLI: error rate 	6 Alert if > 1% for 5m window
- SLI: throughput drop 	6 Alert if RPS drops 40% vs baseline for 5m
- Cost regression: Alert if tokens/request increases > 20% vs baseline sampling over an hour

Data retention / exports
- Default request logs: 30d in our observability layer; we can provide daily export to your S3 bucket for longer retention.

Attachments: I attached a checklist with owners and a proposed kickoff agenda (20270405-redwood_poc_observability_checklist.xlsx).

If that addresses your SRE questions we can lock the kickoff for Wednesday 2027-04-14 2:00pm PST.

Thanks,
